subject: Epoch-boundary token attribution — month-end rollover discrepancy
messages:
From: Samantha Li <billing@nimbushealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vitality.ai>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected charge at month boundary — please investigate

Hi Marissa,

Hope you’re well. We pulled our May invoice and see a ~12% spike vs our daily-average consumption for the last 24 hours of May. The line items point to a large batch of generation tokens that fall exactly at 00:00 UTC on 2027-06-01 in your usage export, but our system shows those requests as completed at 19:59 PT on 2027-05-31.

Can you help explain whether tokens were attributed to the wrong billing day due to an epoch-rollover or timezone conversion? We attached our exported CSV (nimbus_usage_export_202705.csv) and a short trace (sample_session_trace_20270531.txt). This is blocking our AP team from releasing payment until we reconcile.

Thanks — Samantha Li
Billing Operations, Nimbus Health
attachments: nimbus_usage_export_202705.csv (csv), sample_session_trace_20270531.txt (txt)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Li <billing@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected charge at month boundary — please investigate

Hi Samantha — thanks for the heads-up and for the attach. I’ve looped in Ben (billing/instrumentation) and Rafael (account lead) so we can triage quickly.

Initial notes: our pipeline timestamps all tokenized events in epoch milliseconds (UTC) and then bucketizes by UTC date for monthly statements. There is a known edge-case when customers submit very large bulk jobs right around midnight UTC (your trace suggests several long-running generation jobs that finished across the UTC rollover). That can make the visible completion time in your local timezone appear to be before midnight while our UTC bucketing puts activity into the next-day invoice.

Next steps from our side:
- Ben will run a targeted export for your account that includes request_start_ms and request_end_ms for the affected session IDs.
- We’ll generate a corrected per-request ledger and show both UTC-bucketed tokens and your local-time attribution so you can reconcile rows one-to-one.
- If we find an attribution error (e.g., due to delayed write/aggregation), we’ll propose a pro-rata adjustment for the affected window.

We’ll get the targeted export back to you within 24 hours. Apologies for the confusion — Rafael will coordinate timing/credits if required.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Billing Partner, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_epoch_rollover_notes.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samantha Li <billing@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected charge at month boundary — please investigate

On Mon, 31 May 2027 at 10:03, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Initial notes: our pipeline timestamps all tokenized events in epoch milliseconds (UTC) and then bucketizes by UTC date for monthly statements.

Hi Samantha — I pulled the session IDs referenced in your CSV and matched them against our ingestion logs. Summary:

- Several long-running streaming calls opened at 2027-05-31T23:58:45Z and closed at 2027-06-01T00:02:03Z.
- Our billing ledger counts tokens against the UTC date of the final token emission (i.e., 2027-06-01 UTC for those sessions).
- Your local PT clock shows the session completed on 2027-05-31 17:02:03 PST, which creates the visual mismatch.

I attached a short text excerpt (sample_session_trace_20270531.txt) showing request_start_ms and request_end_ms and the per-token counts. I also included guidance in redwood_epoch_rollover_notes.pdf on how we compute bucketization.

Proposal:
1) We can produce a dual-view report that shows tokens by (a) invoice-bucketed UTC day and (b) local-time attribution you can use for AP.
2) For customers who prefer local-day bucketing we can offer a one-time retroactive adjustment for the small set of sessions that straddle the boundary. For Nimbus Health that would reduce the May invoice by ~0.9% (rough estimate) and be processed as a credit on your June statement.

Please confirm whether you want the retro credit or if the dual-view report is sufficient for your reconciliation process.

— Ben Carter
Billing Instrumentation Lead, Redwood Inference
attachments: sample_session_trace_20270531.txt (txt)
From: Samantha Li <billing@nimbushealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@vitality.ai>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 16:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected charge at month boundary — please investigate

Thanks Ben/Marissa — that explanation lines up with what we suspected. Two asks from our AP/Procurement side:

1) Please prepare the dual-view report (UTC vs PT) for the full May 31 window and share as a CSV we can join against our export.
2) We’d like the one-time retroactive adjustment applied (credit on June statement) — Procurement approved the small credit and it’ll help close our PO.

If you can send the report and confirmation of the credit (amount & where it will appear) by EOD Thursday PT, we’ll release payment. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Samantha Li
Billing Operations, Nimbus Health
